Command: Offer two loaves of new grain on Weeks
Summary: On the Feast of Weeks, two wave loaves baked with leaven from the new grain are offered as firstfruits to the LORD.
Commandment: On the Feast of Weeks, offer two wave loaves of fine flour baked with leaven, the firstfruits unto the LORD.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The leavened loaves are the feast's one exception: the harvest offering itself, unlike the Passover bread, could be leavened. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
